ends.title: Goals, values & worthwhile change
ends.summary: What is wanted can change along with the means of achieving it.

obligations.title: Beneficiaries, demands & authority
obligations.summary: Who is served, what is promised, and who may decide remain distinct.

perspectives.title: Attention, interpretation & evidence
perspectives.summary: An accurate account can still omit the distinction that should govern.

possibilities.title: Alternatives & missing operations
possibilities.summary: Change the available possibilities when choosing among them cannot suffice.

connections.title: Parts, handoffs & shared conditions
connections.summary: A working part is useful only through the conditions of its actual connection.

information.title: Observation, memory & action
information.summary: Preserve the distinctions an available action needs at the moment of use.

continuity.title: Arrival, persistence & recovery
continuity.summary: First success, continued service, and recovery after interruption are different.

production.title: Production, support & reproduction
production.summary: Count what creates, sustains, and reproduces the capability.

groups.title: Create the means of continued work
Carry the accomplishment into another use

correction.title: Feedback, repair & revision
correction.summary: A correction needs time, a receiving operation, and compatible dependencies.

inquiry.title: Inquiry, judgment & discovery
inquiry.summary: Choose complete continuations while allowing the purpose and inventory to change.

capability.title: Learning, agency & enabling conditions
capability.summary: What someone knows, feels, wants, can do, and controls need different evidence.

methods.title: Unoptimized mind change & perspective
methods.summary: Locate the omitted contribution and change the work that still omits it.

groups.title: The wrong target or incomplete operation
The effort and correction left to others

ends-and-means.title: A method’s prerequisite need not be the goal’s prerequisite
ends-and-means.summary: Rejecting an unavailable method can preserve the goal and expose a better route.

children.title: One method needs diagnosis
children.text: A sign-repair route inspects two components before choosing a reversal. Those observations are necessary for that route.

children.title: Another method bypasses diagnosis
children.text: For a positive original value and magnitude-preserving transformations, taking the delivered magnitude restores the original directly.

children.title: A goal needs it only if every adequate route does
children.text: “This method requires diagnosis” cannot establish “repair requires diagnosis.” The supplied magnitude operation is a counterexample.

children.title: An objection can target the means
children.text: Do not infer that someone rejects the goal merely because they reject a method, its cost, or its prerequisites. Establish which commitment they reject.

changing-goals.title: Inquiry can discover what is worth wanting
changing-goals.summary: A demand for a settled target can disable the inquiry that would discover one.

children.title: Execute an established change
children.text: The purpose and criterion may already be justified. The missing work can then be a means of execution.

children.title: Discover a worthwhile change
children.text: The question, beneficiary, or criterion may emerge through exploration. Requiring them in advance excludes this undertaking.

children.title: A true starting account can lose authority
children.text: An accurate account of completing accepted requests need not govern an inquiry into whether eligible people receive service.

children.title: A revised criterion is a revised claim
children.text: Retain what the earlier criterion established. Identify what the new question makes relevant instead of reporting a higher score on a different task.

unbundling-values.title: A conflict between bundles can hide compatible commitments
unbundling-values.summary: Separating content, identity, contact, and authority can preserve demands that one bundled action puts in conflict.

children.title: The stipulated obligations
children.text: Make the substance of a dissent available for review; protect the contributor’s identity when identification is unnecessary.

children.title: The initial bundle
children.text: Publishing the dissent together with its author satisfies the first obligation while violating the second. Suppressing both reverses the failure.

children.title: Separate the fields
children.text: Publish the required substantive account; withhold the unnecessary identity and contact route. Under these stated obligations, both demands are met.

children.title: Preserve a real remaining conflict
children.text: If accountable identification is itself required, this separation does not settle the case. Compare that actual obligation; do not declare all values compatible.

benefit-and-effort.title: Less effort does not always mean a better change
benefit-and-effort.summary: Completion, understanding, interest, later reuse, and burdens on others can change the ranking.

children.title: Route A: finish in one unit
children.text: The stipulated task is completed without an additional valued distinction.

children.title: Route B: finish in two units and gain a distinction
children.text: B has more immediate cost and another possible benefit. Completion time alone does not rank the whole consequence.

parts.title: What an efficiency judgment must retain

children.title: Valuation determines the comparison
children.text: If only task completion matters, A wins. If the extra understanding is worth the extra effort, B can win. No common value scale has been supplied merely by counting time.

children.title: Include displaced and later effort
children.text: A short answer can move reconstruction to the reader. A reusable construction can cost more now and save work later, provided the relevant uses occur.

coverage.title: 100% completion can coexist with 10% coverage
coverage.summary: A perfect score over accepted requests can conceal exclusion of the people the service concerns.

children.title: Completion: 10 of 10 accepted requests
children.text: Every accepted request is served, so completion is 100%. This report can be accurate.

children.title: Coverage: 10 of 100 eligible requests
children.text: Ninety eligible requests never enter that denominator. Service reaches only 10% of the relevant requests.

children.title: Repair the governing question
children.text: Ask whether eligible requests are served. More accurate reporting of accepted work alone preserves the exclusion.

children.title: Supply the missing service
children.text: Changing the denominator makes the shortfall visible. Capacity, access, or another actual service route must still address it.

guarantee-scope.title: A guarantee changes when its conditions change
guarantee-scope.summary: One design, one environment, one duration, and one set of requirements define a different claim from all of them.

children.title: One successful case versus every admitted case
children.text: A working instance establishes existence. A universal guarantee must cover every state and disturbance it admits.

children.title: Conditions admitted
children.text: The cases include the relevant environment, disturbance, and operating state. A proof over one admitted set does not settle an enlarged one.

children.title: Once versus continued use
children.text: Arrival at a desired condition does not establish a policy that preserves it through wear, demand, and repair.

children.title: Restricting the admitted conditions
children.text: A valve qualified at one pressure has a narrower claim than a valve qualified across a pressure range. The restriction is substantive.

children.title: Preserving the original obligation
children.text: If excluded circumstances still matter, proving the narrower claim leaves their obligation unresolved. Naming a limit does not discharge it.

permissions.title: A valid instruction does not supply authority
permissions.summary: Correct content, competence, permission, and the ability to withdraw are different conditions.

children.title: Understanding and skill
children.text: A person can understand the instruction and know how to execute it while lacking access or permission.

children.title: A legitimate refusal
children.text: Refusal can preserve a valid concern. Increased compliance would not establish that the undertaking became more worthwhile.

children.title: Effective control over the relevant choice
children.text: Where participation is part of the concern, people need an actual opportunity to understand, question, revise, or decline the arrangement.

children.title: A permission with the right scope
children.text: Authority to inspect does not imply authority to publish or alter. A message about permission does not itself grant permission.

disagreement.title: Different judgments need not be contradictory factual claims
disagreement.summary: Meaning, reference, evidence, values, permissions, and methods can each locate a different disagreement.

children.title: Different question or reference class
children.text: “All requests were completed” can concern accepted requests while “most people were not served” concerns eligible requests. Both can be true.

children.title: Different priorities or authority
children.text: Two people can accept the same calculation while disagreeing about whose burden is permissible or who may decide.

parts.title: Apply a repair to that difference

children.title: Evidence can address a disputed factual premise
children.text: A corrected count changes a count-dependent conclusion. It cannot, by itself, choose a beneficiary or grant authority.

children.title: Do not erase a live difference for coherence
children.text: Retain incompatible demands until an actual alternative, justified decision, or changed condition addresses them. Matching vocabulary does not reconcile them.

representation.title: An organization is adequate for the distinctions it preserves
representation.summary: A subject tree can preserve membership while losing dependencies, evidence, timing, or alternative interpretations.

children.title: A retained distinction
children.text: If two cases need different answers, their representation must keep enough information to distinguish them or recover the distinction.

children.title: A lost distinction
children.text: If a representation makes those cases identical, no decoder using that representation alone can always supply their different answers.

children.title: Several views of one result
children.text: Purpose, mental change, causal dependency, and proof can organize the same canonical result differently. The view changes; the result need not be duplicated.

children.title: More depth is useful only when it carries a relation
children.text: A file name is not a completed leaf. Conversely, inventing further folders after the relevant distinctions are explicit adds no missing knowledge.

scope-of-design.title: A boundary can exclude the variable that repairs the problem
scope-of-design.summary: Nominal dimensions, manufacturing variation, assembly policy, and use conditions expose different interventions.

parts.title: Four scopes of the fit undertaking

children.title: Part dimensions
children.text: Under the original manufacturing variation, no nominal difference satisfies both clearance limits.

children.title: Manufacturing and assembly
children.text: Reducing variation creates a feasible interval. Matching particular pairs changes the admitted joint combinations.

parts.title: The consequences of expanding the scope

children.title: Replacement and environment
children.text: Matched assembly creates a replacement obligation. Environmental drift can defeat a fit that works before use.

children.title: Broader is useful when it changes the live judgment
children.text: Including more causes is not automatically better. Include a boundary’s extra variables when they change an available intervention or a justified conclusion.

shared-evidence.title: Two reports can still supply only one evidential route
shared-evidence.summary: Agreement between copies does not independently check the event they both copy.

children.title: Two dashboards, one event record
children.text: If both reports copy the same mistaken record, their agreement survives the error. Counting them as independent confirmations adds no protection against it.

children.title: Several arguments, one indispensable premise
children.text: Defeating the shared premise defeats these routes to a conclusion without proving that the conclusion is false. Another route may establish it.

children.title: Sincerity, access, competence, permission, reliability
children.text: A sincere speaker can lack direct access. A reliable report can still be unauthorized to disclose. One person-wide trust score loses these differences.

children.title: Check the dependency that could change the answer
children.text: Seek an observation or justification that does not merely reproduce the questioned source. Independence must follow the actual route.

new-operation.title: A new operation can make the old optimum unnecessary
new-operation.summary: The sign-repair optimum falls from cost 3 to cost 1 when the proved magnitude operation enters the available set.

children.title: Original inventory
children.text: Inspecting both sign transformations and then correcting the delivered sign costs 3. A direct reset costs 4. The diagnostic route is optimal in that inventory.

children.title: Supplied operation
children.text: For a positive original value, magnitude-preserving sign transformations leave its magnitude intact. Taking the delivered absolute value restores the original for cost 1.

children.title: Why magnitude is enough
children.text: For original x > 0, the delivered value is either x or −x. Both have absolute value x, so no distinction between the two transformations is needed.

parts.title: The exact boundary of the improvement

children.title: A negative original value is a counterexample
children.text: Absolute value would return a positive value instead of the original negative value. The condition cannot be discarded.

children.title: Change the planner’s inventory
children.text: Better search through the old operations cannot select an absent operation. The receiving planner must admit the construction and its precondition.

variation.title: Changing variation can remove an impossible nominal trade-off
variation.summary: With half-widths 0.010 and 0.015, nominal differences from 0.045 to 0.075 meet both clearance limits.

children.title: Nominal adjustment cannot satisfy both extremes
children.text: With original half-widths 0.040 and 0.050, the nominal gap would need to be at least 0.110 and at most 0.010. No value does both.

children.title: The variable that changes feasibility
children.text: Reducing the combined error half-width to 0.025 yields the nonempty nominal interval 0.045–0.075.

parts.title: A supplied design and its remaining conditions

children.title: Nominal gap 0.060
children.text: The admitted actual clearance is 0.035–0.085 before additional environmental drift. Both stated limits are satisfied.

children.title: Capability and measurement remain distinct
children.text: This derivation specifies needed manufacturing capability. Inspection can discover a part’s dimension; it does not itself reduce production variation.

removing-obstructions.title: Removing an exclusion can enable an existing useful action
removing-obstructions.summary: A new resource is unnecessary when an authorized removal releases the resource or action already needed.

parts.title: Two ways an existing route is blocked

children.title: A rule disables an adequate action
children.text: If the rule is unnecessary and its authorized removal preserves every legitimate condition, removal makes the old mechanism available.

children.title: An irrelevant process holds an exclusive resource
children.text: Ending that process can release the resource for the useful operation. More exhortation does not release it.

children.title: An actual route becomes available
children.text: A relabeling that leaves the same actions disabled does not supply this change. Identify the resource released or exclusion removed.

children.title: Legitimate protections still govern
children.text: Removing a safety or permission condition changes the undertaking. It cannot be credited as satisfying the original conditions merely because action becomes easier.

imagination.title: An accurate account need not remain the governing account
imagination.summary: A new possibility can arise by changing what is being asked, without first proving the original account false.

parts.title: Preserve what the starting account establishes

children.title: Completion within accepted requests
children.text: The original completion count can be entirely correct. Its truth is compatible with the exclusion of eligible requests.

children.title: Optimality within supplied actions
children.text: The sign planner can be exactly optimal. Its proof does not establish that the inventory contains every constructible action.

parts.title: Develop the changed perspective far enough to matter

children.title: Ask about the excluded consequence
children.text: Coverage exposes the unserved requests; taking magnitude constructs a cheaper adequate operation under its positive-source condition.

children.title: A renamed account is insufficient
children.text: The new perspective earns its place through a changed question, distinction, operation, or judgment. Merely labeling it perfected supplies none of these.

interfaces.title: Correct components need compatible receiving conditions
interfaces.summary: Overlap between one component’s outputs and another’s accepted inputs is weaker than guaranteed composition.

children.title: Producer admits outputs from 0 to 10
children.text: The producer can meet its own specification by returning 2.

children.title: Receiver admits inputs from 5 to 15
children.text: The receiver can meet its own specification and still reject 2. Nonempty overlap does not protect every admitted output.

children.title: Restrict or extend a supported range
children.text: Restrict the producer to 5–10, or extend the receiver to accept 0–15, when the undertaking allows the change.

children.title: Supply an actual converter
children.text: A converter must map every relevant output into accepted inputs and be available when needed. Naming an interface leaves this operation unsupplied.

timing.title: Correct contributions can be jointly unavailable in time
timing.summary: Two individually feasible tasks can demand more concurrent capacity than the arrangement supplies.

children.title: Two one-hour tasks in the same hour
children.text: Both require the same exclusive machine throughout their execution. Each task alone fits.

children.title: Their joint demand exceeds supply
children.text: Changing their order cannot fit two exclusive machine-hours into one hour. More consistent instructions leave this arithmetic unchanged.

children.title: Change a causal condition
children.text: A second machine, a longer permitted interval, a faster valid process, or a legitimate requirement revision can alter feasibility.

children.title: Count time until the contribution is usable
children.text: Arrival, interpretation, and necessary support belong to the relevant dependency path. A correct message after the last useful start time does not restore the expired option.

shared-dependency.title: Redundant routes can fail through the same dependency
shared-dependency.summary: If both alternatives require the same unavailable condition, adding the second alternative leaves that failure intact.

children.title: Route A needs a and c; route B needs b and c
children.text: Combined success requires c and at least one of a or b. The second route protects against loss of a or b individually.

children.title: Failure of c defeats both routes
children.text: Two pumps on one unavailable power supply are redundant only with respect to failures their routes actually separate.

children.title: Supply or diversify the common condition
children.text: Inspect the shared power, authorization, source record, or premise before counting independent protection.

children.title: Do not invent independence from names
children.text: Different labels or locations do not establish distinct failure routes. Probability claims require the relevant joint distribution.

composed-corrections.title: Repairing one component can worsen the delivered result
composed-corrections.summary: Two sign reversals cancel; removing just one reversal changes a positive delivery to a negative one.

children.title: End-to-end value only
children.text: With two reversals, the received sign matches the positive original. Correcting only the producer breaks that end-to-end property.

children.title: Each component must preserve sign
children.text: Under this additional obligation, both components need correction. An acceptable final value does not establish their individual conformity.

children.title: Coordinate the affected changes
children.text: A revised convention, range, timing, or authority matters at the consumers that rely on it. A locally working replacement can still be incompatible.

children.title: Revisit what consumed the changed premise
children.text: A correction should reach those dependencies. Unrelated work need not be reopened merely because something changed.

common-action.title: Enough information depends on the action that must succeed
common-action.summary: A distinction is unnecessary for feasibility when one available action works for every case it leaves together.

children.title: Levels 1–4: add 2
children.text: With unknown withdrawal 0, 1, or 2, every next level is still in 1–9.

children.title: Every admitted next level
children.text: The smallest is 1 + 2 − 2 = 1; the largest is 4 + 2 − 0 = 6. Both endpoints lie within 1–9.

children.title: Levels 5–9: add 0
children.text: Every next level is also in 1–9. A low/high reading supplies the complete choice; exact measurement is unnecessary for this guarantee.

children.title: Every admitted next level
children.text: The smallest is 5 + 0 − 2 = 3; the largest is 9 + 0 − 0 = 9. This branch also stays within 1–9.

parts.title: A changed requirement changes the needed distinction

children.title: Reach and preserve 4–6
children.text: The supplied exact-level controller reaches this narrower region within three periods and preserves it. The earlier two-action policy does not establish this result.

parts.title: Adequacy and efficiency answer different questions

children.title: Feasible need not mean least costly
children.text: Further information may permit a cheaper action even when a common adequate action already exists. Compare its cost and the complete continuation.

stale-observation.title: An exact past observation can be inadequate now
stale-observation.summary: The relevant cases are current possibilities, not just the precision of an earlier reading.

children.title: Earlier level: exactly 4
children.text: An intervening withdrawal of 0, 1, or 2 leaves current levels 4, 3, or 2 possible.

children.title: Acting as if 4 were still certain
children.text: Adding 2 followed by another permitted withdrawal can produce a next level as low as 2. The reading’s past accuracy cannot guarantee the narrower band.

parts.title: What can restore a justified choice

children.title: Observe, predict within justified bounds, or change the action
children.text: The controller must cover the remaining current possibilities. Historical precision is not a substitute for that coverage.

children.title: Retain the time and relevant history
children.text: A value detached from its age and intervening changes can lose the distinctions the receiving operation requires.

memory.title: Stored information needs a route back into the relevant use
memory.summary: Retention, retrieval, recognition of applicability, and changed action are separate dependencies.

parts.title: What a stored correction does not guarantee

children.title: Availability in an archive
children.text: The correction can exist without being retrieved at the next decision. More stored copies do not establish timely access.

children.title: Recognition of the applicable condition
children.text: The magnitude repair works for a positive source. Remembering “use absolute value” while losing that condition can reproduce the negative-source failure.

children.title: The trigger and decisive relation
children.text: Keep the positive-source condition with the operation and the negative counterexample. The needed distinction must be recoverable where the operation is selected.

children.title: A changed receiving operation
children.text: An archived correction becomes operational when the affected rule or consumer uses it. File existence alone establishes storage, not uptake or learning.

attention.title: What is visible can determine which question is even available
attention.summary: A working view must expose the distinction needed for the live judgment.

parts.title: Two accurate displays with different consequences

children.title: Accepted requests and completed requests only
children.text: The display can support a correct completion judgment while leaving eligible but unaccepted requests unavailable to inspection.

children.title: Eligible requests beside served requests
children.text: The same undertaking now exposes the coverage shortfall. This supplies a distinction the first view omitted.

children.title: Selection and representation
children.text: Put the consequential comparison in the working view. Merely telling a reader to be more attentive does not supply the missing denominator.

children.title: Perception and interpretation
children.text: Visible marks must carry distinguishable meanings. A parent-child line can show containment; it does not also explain whether one subject causes, supports, or exemplifies another.

arrival-and-preservation.title: Reaching a condition once does not establish continued capability
arrival-and-preservation.summary: A route to a target and a policy that preserves it are different constructions.

children.title: Remove states without a preserving action
children.text: In the finite supplied model, repeatedly retain only states with an available action whose every admitted successor stays in the retained set.

children.title: At the fixed point, preservation follows
children.text: Choosing such an action at each step keeps the state inside the set by induction, while the modeled conditions and action availability continue.

children.title: Expand outward by robust predecessors
children.text: A newly included state has an action sending every successor to an earlier layer. The layer index bounds worst-case steps to the maintainable target.

children.title: An absent action is not a successful action
children.text: An empty successor set cannot certify control by vacuous truth. The construction requires available actions with nonempty admitted outcomes.

stocks-and-support.title: Continued service consumes conditions that must also continue
stocks-and-support.summary: A service-only state can hide the stock, labor, or authority that makes its next action available.

children.title: Battery, part, time, or repair allowance
children.text: Treating the action as always available implicitly supplies replenishment. Without it, the claimed indefinite route may not exist.

children.title: Track the support as part of the state
children.text: For stock b, action cost c, and replenishment r, the next stock is b − c + r. Execution also requires enough stock before the action.

children.title: A joint invariant can be smaller or empty
children.text: A service state that appears maintainable may lose that status when exhausted support is represented.

children.title: Identify the replenishing route
children.text: The relevant question includes who repairs the maintainer, supplies replacement parts, renews access, and remains available during interruption.

service-during-repair.title: No dispatch policy supplies absent concurrent repair labor
service-during-repair.summary: Two stations provide four initial jobs; one fully occupied worker cannot sustain service in the stipulated model.

children.title: Each station serves twice before repair
children.text: Using the two initially ready stations consumes four services of initial capacity.

children.title: All labor serves current demand
children.text: No labor remains for repair while continuous service is required. Reordering dispatch cannot create the missing simultaneous work.

children.title: Two workers can serve and repair concurrently
children.text: One station serves while the other is restored. The resulting finite policy sustains service from eight of nine wear states.

children.title: The invariant behind the eight states
children.text: Unless both stations are fully worn, at least one can serve now. Repairing the other station restores it to ready for the next period, preserving the existence of a station that can serve.

children.title: The excluded starting condition matters
children.text: If both stations are already fully worn, no station can serve immediately. More capable ongoing maintenance does not erase this initial obstruction.

recovery.title: A repair route and uninterrupted service are different guarantees
recovery.summary: Being able to restore operation after an interruption does not establish service during that interruption.

children.title: Remain within the acceptable condition
children.text: This requires an operating route that preserves the condition through the admitted disturbances.

children.title: Leave and later return
children.text: A recovery route can restore a damaged arrangement while allowing a period of unavailable service.

parts.title: What the undertaking requires during repair

children.title: Reserves can cover a bounded interruption
children.text: If each period consumes one reserve unit and repair takes d periods, at least d available units are needed to cover that interval under the stated demand.

children.title: Support the repair itself
children.text: A named recovery plan needs available labor, parts, access, and time. The service requirement determines whether interruption is acceptable.

production-bootstrap.title: A producer’s missing prerequisite changes the investment threshold
production-bootstrap.summary: Including the bootstrap part moves the tooling advantage from two units to four.

children.title: Manual production costs 4n
children.text: Each unit costs four work units.

children.title: Ready tooling costs 5 + n + 2 floor((n−1)/3)
children.text: The tool has setup cost, per-unit work, and periodic maintenance. This ready-tool comparison favors tooling from n = 2.

children.title: The missing bootstrap part costs 4
children.text: The complete tooling route costs 9 + n + 2 floor((n−1)/3). It cannot make its own first required part before it can operate.

children.title: The complete comparison changes
children.text: Manual production is cheaper for one or two units; the routes tie at three; complete tooling is cheaper from four onward.

production-horizon.title: The best first result can choose the worse continuing arrangement
production-horizon.summary: A capability investment can be worthwhile through its continuation despite lower immediate output.

children.title: One finished unit
children.text: The full tooling route costs more than manual production for a single unit.

children.title: A known run of four or more units
children.text: Including bootstrap and periodic maintenance, the tooling route costs less across the full stipulated run.

children.title: It rejects the enabling step
children.text: Tool construction produces no finished service unit immediately. A rule requiring each step to improve current output excludes the investment.

children.title: Actual continuation governs the gain
children.text: Future uses, deadlines, loss of usefulness, support costs, and valued learning can change a reuse comparison. Hypothetical infinite reuse does not settle a finite undertaking.

reproduction.title: A repeatable artifact can still depend on an unrepeatable contribution
reproduction.summary: An expert’s hidden adjustment belongs to the production arrangement when each successful use needs it.

children.title: The demonstration’s environment
children.text: A sample output can rely on its author’s access, judgment, local data, manual correction, or unavailable tooling.

children.title: The next recipient’s arrangement
children.text: Copying the artifact does not copy those contributions. Successful use by the original author does not establish independent reproduction.

parts.title: What a complete reproduction route supplies

children.title: Make the necessary contribution usable
children.text: Implement the operation, supply the dependency, or retain a qualified available maintainer with its cost and limits.

children.title: Distinguish support from recipient learning
children.text: A person can perform well with a supplied tool while lacking the unsupported skill. Both can be valuable, but they are different accomplishments.

transfer.title: A result transfers through its premises, not its vocabulary
transfer.summary: The same dependency can support a deduction in another setting when the receiving case actually satisfies it.

children.title: Shared indispensable condition
children.text: Two physical routes and two arguments can share the Boolean pattern “both require c.” Failure of c defeats those routes in either case.

children.title: The receiving facts must establish that pattern
children.text: Calling both cases systems does not prove that their conditions, authority, uncertainty, or mechanisms agree.

children.title: Mechanisms and observed effects
children.text: A proof about a finite water controller supplies no measurement of human understanding or physical pump performance. Those claims need their own receiving evidence.

children.title: Recheck a changed condition
children.text: Different disturbances, duration, beneficiaries, permissions, or available actions can invalidate the original use while leaving the original deduction intact.

feedback-deadline.title: Feedback after the last useful start time cannot restore an expired option
feedback-deadline.summary: Correct content can arrive too late to change the action it was meant to support.

children.title: The corrective action must start by 09:20
children.text: After that time, the available action cannot meet the live deadline.

children.title: The accurate report arrives at 09:25
children.text: Even immediate comprehension leaves the report five minutes late. Better wording alone cannot restore the expired action.

children.title: Change when the information becomes usable
children.text: Earlier detection, an earlier report, or a justified action requiring less remaining time can alter the result. Each needs its actual route.

children.title: Change a legitimate timing condition
children.text: A revised deadline or continuing reserve can create another opportunity when authorized and feasible. The original deadline was still missed.

correction-propagation.title: A correction matters at the operations that consume it
correction-propagation.summary: A stored critique leaves the next result unchanged when the generator still uses the defeated rule.

children.title: A rule produces a recommendation
children.text: If the rule is unchanged, adding a critique elsewhere does not alter the recommendation.

children.title: A generated view consumes source data
children.text: Fixing a source file without regenerating its dependent view can leave the recipient using the old content.

children.title: Change or restrict the active producer
children.text: Replace the defeated rule, preserve its valid conditions, and update the consumers whose conclusions rely on it.

children.title: Keep the counterexample with its trigger
children.text: The positive-source magnitude repair and the negative-source failure must travel together. A correction that drops applicability can generate a new error.

replaceability.title: A qualified pair does not establish interchangeable replacement
replaceability.summary: Matched assembly can work while arbitrary replacement violates the relationship that made it work.

children.title: Every independently admitted pair
children.text: A guarantee of free interchangeability must cover the Cartesian product of the allowed component ranges.

children.title: Only selected matched pairs
children.text: A matching rule can admit a smaller joint set. A successful particular pair establishes the relation for that pair.

children.title: A replacement must preserve the pairing condition
children.text: A component working in isolation can fail with the retained counterpart. Replacement selection must recover the required joint fit.

children.title: Carry the receiving conditions into maintenance
children.text: Dimensions, identifiers, conventions, timing, and authority can all be parts of the receiving relation. “Working replacement” is incomplete without them.

whole-route.title: The next useful contribution depends on complete continuations
whole-route.summary: A question is valuable through the later actions it makes possible, not simply the information it returns.

children.title: Compare intervention with inquiry branches
children.text: For each available inquiry, include its cost and the best valid continuation for every possible answer. Compare this with available common repairs.

children.title: Return an executable conditional route
children.text: The supplied planner chooses actual inquiries and repairs for explicit cases, operations, outcomes, and costs. A field saying “select the mechanism” would leave that work undone.

parts.title: The limit is part of the result

children.title: An inseparable obstruction
children.text: If available inquiries cannot separate cases and no common intervention repairs them, the planner returns that obstruction rather than a fictitious successful plan.

children.title: The inventory remains revisable
children.text: A newly constructed action or an omitted case changes the selection problem. The original optimum is conditional on what was admitted.

information-cost.title: More information can lead to a more costly repair
information-cost.summary: The calculation case finishes in 2 work units; the more informative first inspection leads to 3.

children.title: Restore usable calculation output
children.text: The value of an observation depends on which repair it enables and what the complete route costs.

children.title: The better first inquiry
children.text: The supplied case construction identifies the relevant repair with total cost 2. Beginning with the higher-information layout inquiry costs 3 without improving repaired outputs.

children.title: Reuse what is already known
children.text: When the relevant context is supplied in advance, repeating that inquiry adds cost. The needed next contribution changes.

children.title: Revise an incomplete case set
children.text: A previously omitted possible answer invalidates the old coverage. Admitting it requires recomputing the affected plan, not continuing under the earlier case inventory.

intermediate-inquiry.title: A step with no immediate recommendation change can still be necessary
intermediate-inquiry.summary: Requiring immediate improvement from every observation rejects both first steps of a better diagnostic route.

children.title: A single inspection does not settle the repair
children.text: The other transformation can still reverse the sign. Either first observation alone leaves the final repair choice unresolved.

children.title: Both inspections support a cheaper route
children.text: The pair followed by correction costs 3, compared with a reset costing 4. The first question matters through the second.

parts.title: Two distinct corrections to the method

children.title: Compare the complete continuation
children.text: Do not discard an enabling question merely because its immediate recommendation is unchanged.

children.title: Then reconsider the inventory itself
children.text: The positive-source magnitude operation costs 1 and bypasses both inspections. Defending the better old route must not block constructing a better new one.

knowing-and-doing.title: Understanding a method does not supply every condition for action
knowing-and-doing.summary: Skill, instruments, time, access, collaboration, and control can each be a different missing contribution.

children.title: Knowledge is absent
children.text: A usable explanation, demonstration, or practice may supply a needed distinction or operation. Its effect on this person still needs observation.

children.title: Knowledge is present but execution is blocked
children.text: Understanding two exclusive one-hour tasks cannot complete both in the same available hour. Explanation does not supply the absent time.

children.title: Supply the instrument, access, resource, or coordination
children.text: A correctly identified permission gap remains a gap until the relevant authority grants access or an adequate authorized route is available.

children.title: Keep the person and their conditions in view
children.text: Capability can belong to a person with tools and support. Attributing every shortfall to belief or intelligence omits those routes.

learning-and-support.title: Supported performance and retained skill are different accomplishments
learning-and-support.summary: A supplied operation can complete the task without establishing what the recipient can later do unaided.

children.title: An aid performs the operation
children.text: A working planner can supply a valid finite route for its admitted cases. This is a property of the supplied arrangement.

children.title: A person learns the operation
children.text: Retained discrimination, execution, and later recall concern the person’s capability. Successful output with the aid does not by itself establish those changes.

children.title: Continued supported capability
children.text: Keep the aid, access, data, maintenance, and correction route available when they are part of the intended arrangement.

children.title: Later independent use or transfer
children.text: If independence or use in a changed context matters, inspect that performance and its conditions. Removing support without this distinction can remove the demonstrated capability.

motivation.title: Rejecting a method does not establish rejection of the goal
motivation.summary: An objection, a lack of resources, and a lack of willingness call for different contributions.

children.title: “I will not use this route”
children.text: The objection can concern cost, permission, feasibility, burden, or a better alternative while preserving the desired end.

children.title: “I want the result but cannot act”
children.text: Motivation does not supply unavailable time, access, skill, or equipment. More encouragement need not change the obstruction.

children.title: Investigate the stated objection
children.text: If an objection identifies absent repair labor, the plan needs a capability correction. Increased enthusiasm does not sustain the service.

children.title: Do not infer a person’s inner state from task output alone
children.text: Observed nonperformance under a blocked arrangement is compatible with willingness. The conditions and the person’s report need distinct consideration.

emotion.title: A feeling, its interpretation, and the condition behind it are different targets
emotion.summary: Reappraisal cannot be credited with repairing an external condition it leaves unchanged.

children.title: A person reports a feeling
children.text: That report concerns experience. It does not by itself establish the causal explanation, the external condition, or an improvement.

children.title: An interpretation changes
children.text: A changed interpretation can matter to experience or action. It does not itself grant access, preserve a contribution, or restore unavailable capacity.

children.title: If a contribution was lost, restore it where possible
children.text: Preserving the actual work is a different operation from asking its author to feel better about the loss.

children.title: If experience is the concern, attend to experience
children.text: External repair can be valuable without establishing emotional change. Neither accomplishment should be silently substituted for the other.

agreement.title: Less agreement can be the beneficial change
agreement.summary: An objection that reveals a missing necessary condition can improve the undertaking by defeating an infeasible plan.

children.title: A plan gains support
children.text: Confidence and adoption can increase while the plan still lacks concurrent repair labor. Agreement does not change the service capacity.

children.title: A justified objection reduces support
children.text: Pointing out that absence makes the adopted plan less defensible. Under a concern for sustainable service, that changed judgment is useful.

parts.title: The recipient of correction can change

children.title: Revise the plan or its conditions
children.text: Supply concurrent repair or another demonstrated adequate arrangement. Persuading the objector to assent leaves the obstruction intact.

children.title: Preserve informed agency
children.text: A person’s ability to question, decline, or revise can itself matter. Predictable compliance cannot stand in for that capability.

completed-operation.title: A framework is incomplete when it names the decisive operation but does not supply it
completed-operation.summary: “Choose enough observations and a suitable controller” still leaves the selection task with the recipient.

children.title: An instruction names the intended result
children.text: A schema containing “diagnose,” “select,” or “improve” can be complete as a document while leaving its central operation unperformed.

children.title: The recipient still has to construct the answer
children.text: If the person lacks that method, the instruction alone has not supplied the usable capability.

children.title: Observe whether the level is at most 4
children.text: Add 2 when it is; otherwise add 0. Under the stated withdrawals, this policy preserves levels 1–9.

children.title: Keep the proof and scope available
children.text: The construction removes a specific mathematical selection task. It does not establish that a reader understood, remembered, adopted, or benefited from it.

usable-consequence.title: A shorter contribution can leave more work before it is useful
usable-consequence.summary: Efficiency includes interpretation, reconstruction, missing support, and the time remaining for action.

children.title: Sequential dependencies
children.text: If arrival, interpretation, and support take successive times, their sum determines when the contribution becomes usable. Overlap requires the actual dependency path instead.

children.title: A short but unfinished answer
children.text: Omitting the decisive inference can save reading while adding more reconstruction. Word count alone cannot rank total recipient effort.

children.title: The consequence with its decisive conditions
children.text: Show what changes in the judgment and why. Keep a condition or counterexample beside the operation it qualifies.

children.title: Actual human effects remain a separate observation
children.text: Static availability establishes that content is supplied. It does not measure comprehension time, later recall, benefit, or a universal optimum.

symbolic-bounds.title: Unknown values can still permit an exact design bound
symbolic-bounds.summary: A missing measurement need not leave the mathematical consequence unfinished.

children.title: Requirement and admitted error
children.text: For y = ax + e, a > 0, e between e_min and e_max, and requirement y ≤ b, the worst error is e_max.

children.title: The robust bound
children.text: Every admitted error satisfies the requirement exactly when x ≤ (b − e_max) / a. No observed value of e is needed to derive this region.

children.title: Uncertain positive coefficient
children.text: If a is between a_min and a_max and x ≥ 0, use a_max in the worst case. For negative x the worst coefficient is a_min; ignoring the sign changes the answer.

children.title: A normative parameter is still a decision
children.text: If b is an unchosen value judgment, the formula does not choose b. It distinguishes the completed conditional deduction from the decision that remains.

history-and-action.title: Remembered history can supply a distinction absent from the current observation
history-and-action.summary: A failure of memoryless control need not establish a failure of every controller.

children.title: Initially distinguish two persistent modes
children.text: The mode is L or R and never changes. An initial observation reveals it; every later observation is the same ready signal.

children.title: The required action depends on the mode
children.text: Action L succeeds only in mode L; action R succeeds only in mode R. No one action succeeds in both modes.

children.title: Current observation alone is insufficient
children.text: Both modes now look ready, so a memoryless choice based on that reading alone must choose the same action and fail in one mode.

children.title: The retained initial mode supplies the action
children.text: Choose the action named by the remembered mode. It succeeds at every later step because mode persistence is a premise. A changing or forgotten mode defeats this guarantee.

parts.title: The premise that can defeat the remembered answer

children.title: Unobserved mode change
children.text: If the mode changes from L to R after the initial reading, retaining L selects the wrong action. The guarantee needs either persistence or another justified way to detect that change.

reserve-and-dependence.title: A reserve must cover the admitted joint demand and repair duration
reserve-and-dependence.summary: Independent worst-case bounds can demand more reserve than the actual joint possibilities require.

parts.title: The interruption that must be covered

children.title: Constant demand and repair duration
children.text: With demand rate d > 0, duration τ, and no replenishment during repair, preserving service requires and is guaranteed by reserve B ≥ dτ.

children.title: Both independent maxima are admitted together
children.text: If d_max and τ_max can occur jointly, B ≥ d_max τ_max is both sufficient and necessary under the stated constant-rate model.

parts.title: The dependence that changes the answer

children.title: The maxima cannot occur together
children.text: The exact requirement is B ≥ max(dτ) over the admitted joint set. Multiplying separate maxima can overstate the needed reserve.

children.title: Change a relevant causal quantity
children.text: More reserve, lower demand, faster repair, or an adequate alternate route can change the comparison. Favorable averages do not establish coverage of the worst admitted interruption.

mind-change.title: What changes in a mind
mind-change.summary: These are different targets and dependencies of change. Each opens the same result used in the main organization.

dependencies.title: What depends on what
dependencies.summary: Prerequisites, shared support, timing, and correction are causal relations. They can cross branches and form cycles.

claims-and-cases.title: What establishes which claim
claims-and-cases.summary: General relations, stipulated cases, supplied operations, and observed human changes support different conclusions.

groups.title: Claims an output does not establish
